chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil and Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The blood money (diya) is ten thousand dirhams or one thousand dinars.
Jamil said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood money (diya) is one hundred camels.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya: the blood money or financial compensation paid to the family of a homicide victim or to an injured person; a fundamental institution of Islamic criminal law
key_terms.الْإِبِل: Al-ibil: camels; the traditional primary unit for calculating diya in pre-Islamic and early Islamic law
key_terms.دِرْهَم: Dirham: a silver coin used as currency in the early Islamic period
key_terms.دِينَار: Dinar: a gold coin used as currency in the early Islamic period

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of blood money (diya) according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies the diya (blood money) for homicide as either ten thousand dirhams or one thousand dinars in monetary terms. The narrator Jamil then records a second statement of the Imam giving the traditional camel-based measure of one hundred camels. This dual specification reflects the jurisprudential principle that diya can be paid in various equivalent forms — camels being the original standard from pre-Islamic Arabia, with monetary equivalents set for urban contexts where camels were not readily accessible.
